extracted.intended_audience: investors, corporate reporters, sustainability professionals, regulators, and general readers interested in ESG reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and principles for developing and applying Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB) industry-specific standards so companies can disclose investor-focused, decision-useful sustainability (ESG) information with rigor, comparability, and global applicability. Also covers SASB's procedures for research, stakeholder consultation, and alignment with other reporting frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global Applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Investor-focused sustainability 'information should be relevant, reliable and comparable across companies on a global basis.' More than three-quarters of SASB metrics are appropriate for use by companies and investors globally, with remaining metrics under review to enhance global applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SASB encourages companies worldwide to report using SASB disclosure topics and metrics across disclosure channels (annual reports, financial filings, company websites, sustainability reports). The standard-setter actively reviews metrics to increase their international applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Materiality
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB Standards are geared toward providing decision-useful information to investors; evidence of financial materiality is the underpinning for the standards. 'SASB states that its standards focus on “financially material issues because our mission is to help businesses around the world report on the sustainability topics that matter most to their investors.”'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards prioritize sustainability issues that have clear links to a firm's financial performance and shareholder value. This investor-driven materiality focus distinguishes SASB from frameworks (e.g., GRI) that emphasize broader societal impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-Specific Standard-Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB has developed a unique standard for each industry because sustainability issues manifest differently due to differences in business models, resource dependencies, and other factors. SASB developed standards for 77 industries across 11 sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards identify the ESG issues most likely to be material within a given industry; for each industry only a small set (often five or six) of disclosure topics are identified as disclosure priorities. Use of industry-specific standards reduces reporting burden for investor audiences by focusing on the issues most relevant to that industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-Based Research
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB identifies sustainability risks and opportunities for which clear evidence exists that companies in an industry are financially impacted and investors are interested in those impacts. SASB standards are designed to generate standardized and comparable data, which is typically quantitative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SASB 'performs evidence-based research and industry vetting to identify the likely material issues' and 'identif[ies] metrics that companies can use to disclose performance on these issues.' The standards average five topics and 14 metrics (79 percent quantitative) per industry. Independent academic research (e.g., Harvard Business School study) has been used to validate the framework's effectiveness in distinguishing financially material sustainability factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market-Informed Process
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB standards are formulated and vetted using a balance of perspectives from investors, corporate professionals and subject-matter experts. Market input helps SASB leverage commonly used metrics from existing frameworks and regulations to ensure the standards are cost-effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Standards Advisory Group (SAG) and Investor Advisory Group provide market perspectives and implementation guidance. Market-informed choices typically result in a compact list of issues per industry and encourage use of metrics familiar to reporting companies and investors to reduce implementation cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-Useful Disclosure Qualities: Relevant, Reliable, Comparable
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB's mission notes investor-focused sustainability 'information should be relevant, reliable and comparable across companies on a global basis.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards and metrics are designed to produce disclosures that investors can use in financial analysis (relevance), that are prepared with sufficient rigor and controls to be dependable (reliability), and that allow comparison across companies (comparability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard-Setting Due Process
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB's Rules of Procedure describe a due process involving the systematic, independent evaluation of evidence-based research, stakeholder consultation, proposed updates, public comment, and ratification—all of which are subject to public transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SASB uses a project-based model (issue-by-issue) allowing targeted updates for priority themes, regulatory changes, and market trends. Historical versions and associated evidence are archived publicly. The Rules of Procedure govern roles, composition, and operating procedures of the Standards Board to ensure governance integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company Reporting Rigor and Internal Controls
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB recommends that companies use the same level of rigor and internal controls as used for traditional financial measures when reporting sustainability-related performance to investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ensure quality and investor confidence, SASB encourages corporations to apply financial-reporting-grade processes (e.g., data controls, assurance by auditors where appropriate). Examples cited include companies embedding SASB-based sustainability reports in SEC filings and obtaining auditor review or examination reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative, Standardized, Comparable Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB standards aim to identify metrics companies can use to disclose performance; these metrics are standardized, comparable across companies in an industry, and are typically quantitative (SASB standards average 14 metrics per industry, 79% quantitative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because metrics are intended to be quantitative and standardized, they support cross-company comparative analysis, index construction, and integration into financial decision-making. The standards' metric design also facilitates licensing and use by data providers and index creators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainable Industry Classification System (SICS®)
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB's Sustainable Industry Classification System® (SICS®) organizes industries using a combination of traditional classification factors and sustainability risks and opportunities; it classifies companies based on common sustainability issues to identify disclosure topics that are likely to impact all or most companies in an industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SICS groups companies whose sustainability issues are similar even if they are split across traditional industry taxonomies (e.g., hardware categories), and a lookup tool is provided to identify industry classification for companies. The classification underpins selection of disclosure topics and metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment and Complementarity with Other Frameworks (TCFD, GRI, CDSB)
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB collaborates with other sustainability reporting organizations to provide complementary approaches; for example, SASB and CDSB created guidance for TCFD implementation and SASB and GRI are described as having complementary strengths ('GRI looks at the company’s impacts on the world and the SASB looks at the world’s impacts on the company').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SASB participates in mapping and alignment initiatives (e.g., Better Alignment Project, Corporate Reporting Dialogue) to identify commonalities and differences, refine overlapping disclosures, and improve cross-framework interoperability. Companies are advised to use SASB with TCFD guidance for effective climate-related disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project-Based Updates and Prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB uses a project-based model, approaching updates to the standards on an issue-by-issue basis rather than updating all standards at once, allowing it to address priority broad themes, regulatory changes, and market trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach focuses limited standard-setting resources on topics warranting action as identified through research and market consultation; active projects are listed publicly on SASB's website and follow the Rules of Procedure for public consultation and ratification.
